_about: Voltage-register encodings of small I2C PMICs that phones put beside the SoC's own PMICs (camera and display supplies). A port's driver writes these registers itself, so one wrong step size is a wrong voltage with no error anywhere (r5q Test 427: S2MPB03 LDO3 written as 0x80|0 = 0.70 V where the sensor's analog 1.8 V was meant). Fields: reg = the LDO's control register; min_uv + step_uv * (value & vsel_mask); enable = {reg, bit} (reg the same as the control register when the enable bit is in it). Sources: each chip's Linux driver header, cited per chip. Add a chip: copy one, cite its header, run pmic_ldo.py selftest.

s2mpb03.source: Samsung kernel include/linux/regulator/s2mpb03.h (S2MPB03_REG_LDO1_CTRL 0x03 .. LDO7 0x09; [7] enable, [6:0] voltage); checked on r5q (Tests 342, 427)

s2dos05.source: Samsung kernel include/linux/regulator/s2dos05.h (S2DOS05_REG_EN 0x03: bit n-1 = LDOn, bit 4 buck; LDOn config 0x03+n: [6:0] voltage, [7] fast discharge); checked on r5q (touch supplies, redwood_sec_ts.c)
